title: Comparison of effect of cafetière and filtered coffee on serum concentrations of liver aminotransferases and lipids: six month randomised controlled trial
authors: Urgert R, Meyboom S, Kuilman M, Rexwinkel H, Vissers MN, Klerk M, et al.
followUp: 24 weeks of treatment after a 4-week run-in, then 12 weeks of follow-up
population: Healthy men and women aged 19 to 69 recruited through advertisements, Wageningen Agricultural University, the Netherlands; 53 allocated by coin toss after run-in, 46 completed (22 cafetière, 24 filtered coffee)
funder: Netherlands Heart Foundation through the Netherlands Organisation of Scientific Research (grant No 900-562-091).
result: Participants drank 0.9 litres a day of strong cafetière or paper-filtered coffee (Douwe Egberts Roodmerk). Cafetière coffee provided 38 (SD 6) mg cafestol and 33 (5) mg kahweol a day; filtered coffee less than 1 mg of either. After 24 weeks LDL cholesterol was raised by 0.26 mmol/l (95% CI 0.04 to 0.47; P = 0.03), 9% over baseline, relative to filtered coffee; LDL rose 9-14% during treatment; HDL cholesterol was not affected. Triglycerides rose 26% within 2 weeks and 7% at 24 weeks. Alanine aminotransferase rose by up to 80%, and by 9 U/l (3 to 15), 45%, at 24 weeks; it exceeded the upper limit of normal at least once in 8 of 22 cafetière and 1 of 24 filtered-coffee drinkers. All increases were reversible after the intervention stopped.
